name: Hudson Valley Lighting Group
old_description: Residential/commercial lighting manufacturer (Hudson Valley, Troy, Corbett, Mitzi brands)
about:
Hudson Valley Lighting Group (HVLG) operates from Wappingers Falls, New York. The company was founded by David Littman, who serves as CEO. Littman's early exposure to antiques through his mother's "treasure hunts" shaped a philosophy that beautiful objects transform everyday experience.

HVLG designs and manufactures residential and commercial lighting across seven distinct brands: Hudson Valley Lighting, Troy Lighting, Corbett Lighting, Mitzi, CSL, Sonneman, and Schoolhouse. The portfolio spans decorative fixtures — chandeliers, sconces, pendants, lamps — and architectural systems including recessed downlights, cylinders, and modular platforms such as Sonneman's Suspenders® and Constellation® lines. The CSL brand emphasizes patented adjustability and advanced optical systems for performance-driven applications. Beyond lighting, the Schoolhouse brand extends into textiles, furnishings, hardware, and furniture.

The group serves interior designers, specifiers, architects, and builders through dedicated trade and contract-hospitality programs. Its products are specified in residential, commercial, and hospitality projects across North America and, via CE-marked offerings, in European and UK markets.

HVLG positions itself as a creative partner rather than a mere supplier, citing the industry's most comprehensive selection as its differentiator. The company's founding impulse was to make well-designed, well-made lighting and home goods accessible — whether through Corbett's luxurious statement pieces, Mitzi's attainable high design, or Schoolhouse's considered, lasting objects.

name: Hyundai Mobis Alabama, LLC.
old_description: Hyundai Motor Manufacturing Alabama and Kia Motor Manufacturing Georgia.
about:
Hyundai Mobis Alabama, LLC was established in 2002 on nearly 83 acres in Montgomery, Alabama. The company operates as a subsidiary of Hyundai MOBIS, the parts and service arm for South Korean automakers Hyundai Motor Company, Genesis Motors, and Kia Motors. It was created to serve as the largest Tier 1 supplier to Hyundai Motor Manufacturing Alabama (HMMA) and Kia Motor Manufacturing Georgia (KMMG).

The facility spans a 600,000-square-foot plastics plant where injection molding produces front and rear bumpers, instrument panel frames, and after-service parts. Bumpers are molded and painted in-house. A neighboring module plant assembles cockpit (dashboard) modules and front and rear chassis modules using parts from Tier 2 and 3 suppliers. The site also houses a Redistribution Center that ships genuine Hyundai and Kia service parts to dealerships, auto parts stores, and distribution centers across North America.

The company serves the automotive industry exclusively, delivering just-in-sequence modules to HMMA and KMMG for final vehicle assembly. Its Redistribution Center supports the aftermarket by supplying parts to dealerships and retailers nationwide. Customers include the two vehicle assembly plants and the broader North American dealer network.

Hyundai Mobis Alabama emphasizes just-in-sequence delivery, in-house molding and painting, and modular system integration to reduce vehicle weight, part count, and assembly complexity. The operation holds ISO 14001 and IATF 16949 certifications and follows the Hyundai Motor Group's core values of customer focus, challenge, collaboration, people, and globality.

name: I-Chips
old_description: NAB Show 2026: IP00C335 Functional Demo at Macnica Americas Booth.
about:
I-Chips Technology Inc. was founded in 2000 and is headquartered in San Jose, California. The company operates as a fabless semiconductor supplier specializing in video-processing LSI and FPGA-based board products. No founders or ownership details are disclosed in the available sources.

The product line centers on image-processing LSI devices: scaler, de-interlacer/scaler, cross-point switch, and warping/edge-blending chips, several with integrated memory for 4K and 8K resolutions. Recent releases include the IP00C335 4K multi-input/output de-interlacer/scaler with built-in memory, the IP00C241 memory-less scaler for 4K60Hz, the IP00C251 3×3 cross-point switch for 4K60Hz, and the iEB-KXU2 FPGA board supporting HDMI 4K60Hz input and output. The company also offers FPGA boards for prototyping and integration.

I-Chips targets the broadcast and professional AV markets, as evidenced by its demonstration of the IP00C335 at the 2026 NAB Show on the Macnica Americas booth. Its components are designed for OEMs and system integrators building 4K/8K video walls, projection mapping, and real-time video conversion equipment.

The company has not publicly stated a founding mission or specific competitive differentiators beyond its product specifications.

name: I-Pull
old_description: Search our in-stock vehicles to ensure you find the part you need.
about:
I-Pull by Intermountain Auto operates a self-service automotive salvage yard at 3015 North 15th East in Idaho Falls, Idaho. The company describes itself as southeastern Idaho's first self-service salvage yard, though a founding year is not publicly stated. Ownership structure and founder names have not been disclosed.

The yard allows customers to enter for a $2 per-person fee, bring their own hand or battery-powered tools, and remove parts directly from vehicles staged on site. Free equipment includes wheelbarrows, engine hoists, and manual tire-breakdown machines. I-Pull also purchases cars, trucks, vans, and SUVs in any condition, running or not. A daily-updated online inventory lets visitors search for specific vehicles before arriving. Pricing follows a published parts pricelist; core charges apply to certain components and can be refunded within 15 days with a receipt. General returns receive store credit within 30 days.

The business serves DIY mechanics, independent repair shops, and vehicle owners seeking affordable replacement parts. Its inventory spans all makes and models, supporting the automotive repair and auto-recycling sectors in the region.

The self-service model was introduced to give customers direct access to low-cost used parts without the markup of traditional counter sales. By eliminating labor charges for part removal, the yard positions itself as a cost-driven alternative for budget-conscious repair work.

name: I.C. Medical Inc.
old_description: provides increased surgical site visibility for your surgeons while reducing accidental fluid and tissue suction.
about:
I.C. Medical Inc. is headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. The company traces its origins to 1983, when Ioan and Elena Cosmescu emigrated from Romania and settled in Phoenix. Six years later, the couple launched I.C. Medical, establishing a business focused on surgical smoke evacuation. Ioan Cosmescu, a biomedical engineer and inventor, and Elena Cosmescu, a registered nurse and hospital administrator, brought deep healthcare experience to the venture.

Today, I.C. Medical develops and manufactures a range of surgical smoke evacuation devices, including the Crystal Vision® filtration system, the Telescopic PenEvac® and Non-Telescopic PenEvac® electrocautery pencils, as well as filters, sensors, and accessories. All products are produced, assembled, tested, and quality-assured in-house at the company’s 60,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Phoenix. The operation maintains total control over design, engineering, component sourcing, precision manufacturing, and packaging.

The company’s devices are used in surgical operating rooms worldwide, serving hospitals and surgical teams. I.C. Medical’s PenEvac® pencils are compatible with major smoke evacuator brands such as ConMed, Buffalo Filter, Stryker, Neptune, and Zimmer Biomet. The Crystal Vision® system is designed for open surgical procedures, while the PenEvac® line captures smoke at the source during electrosurgery.

I.C. Medical emphasizes its in-house production model as a differentiator, citing the risks of quality fade associated with outsourcing. The company holds 53 U.S. patents and more than 59 international patents for its smoke evacuation technologies. Its quality system is subject to regular audits by the FDA, ISO, CE, and CSA, and all products are made in the United States using virgin raw materials and proprietary processes.

name: I.P.W. Auto Parts
old_description: What eventually started by Peter Tetzlaff out of the back of his van, now has evolved into it's very own location that has stayed in the family for the last 40 years.
about:
I.P.W. Auto Parts operates from a single location at 12040 W Feerick St in Wauwatosa, Wisconsin. The business traces its roots to Peter Tetzlaff, who began selling parts out of the back of his van; the operation has remained family-owned for roughly 40 years. Today the company is run by Sean and Mark Tetzlaff, with Kevin Stachowiak handling sales.

The store functions as a retail and wholesale outlet for automotive parts and supplies. Its inventory spans replacement parts, shop supplies, tires, oils and chemicals, and tools. Brand lines carried include Firestone, IronHead, Mastercraft, and Thunderer tires, along with a range of lubricants, cleaners, fillers, and primers. Customers can browse and purchase through an online catalog that supports vehicle-specific searches, as well as at the physical counter.

The customer base encompasses both do-it-yourself mechanics and professional repair facilities throughout the Greater Milwaukee area. The company emphasizes wholesale pricing for trade customers while maintaining a neighborhood-shop atmosphere for walk-in buyers.

The founders' original vision centered on family values and accessible pricing. The current leadership continues that ethos with the stated motto, "Our family comes first, and you're family," positioning the business as a genuine local alternative to larger chain retailers.

about:
ICOMM Technologies Inc. was founded in 1998 and is headquartered in Malvern, Pennsylvania. The fabless semiconductor company operates from an office Suite 210, and focuses on the design and development of wireless baseband processors for evolving mobile communication standards.

The company provides full custom ASIC design services and partners with back-end design house ICNexus and wafer foundry Fujitsu in Asia to deliver 90 nm and finer geometry ASIC design and fabrication. Its core expertise lies in 3G, 4G, and 5G baseband processor development, including beamforming, beamsteering, and array antenna technologies for 5G networks. ICOMM also conducts research into green energy technology for next-generation wireless systems.

ICOMM serves the wireless communications industry, supplying baseband processor solutions for smartphones, business automation, and autonomous vehicle applications. Its ASIC design and foundry services cater to semiconductor companies seeking low-cost, low-power, high-quality silicon with quick turnaround. The company's green energy R&D targets sustainable technology for future mobile networks.

ICOMM differentiates itself through its fabless model combined with established Asian foundry partnerships, enabling deep submicron capabilities without owning fabrication facilities. The company emphasizes low-cost, low-power, high-quality ASIC services with rapid delivery, and positions itself as a leader in 5G baseband processor innovation.

name: IMPERIALE WOODWORK LLC
old_description: "Rest assured your complete satisfaction will never be compromised."
about:
Imperiale Woodwork LLC operates from Milford, Connecticut, where founder Vinicius Manerba opened the business to the public in early 2016. Manerba had spent roughly a decade specializing in furniture and hardwood flooring before launching the company, which focuses on custom, hand-crafted heirloom pieces.

The shop produces custom furniture with a concentration on live edge tables — dining, conference, and occasional tables — using hundreds of locally sourced hardwood slabs kept in stock. Each piece is hand crafted, from slab selection through final finishing, with an emphasis on preserving the natural character of the wood.

The company serves clients seeking one-of-a-kind tables for residential and commercial settings, including homeowners, designers, and businesses furnishing conference rooms. Projects are collaborative, with the team working directly with customers to match slabs to specific design visions.

Imperiale Woodwork was founded on the mission of saving fallen trees and returning them to life as functional furniture. Manerba describes the work as a passion for live edge design and a commitment to creating pieces that can be passed down through generations.

name: INANOVATE
old_description: Lyme-ID is the most sensitive Lyme disease blood test cleared by the FDA–soon to be available.
about:
Inanovate is based in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. The company develops and manufactures Lyme-ID, an FDA 510(k)-cleared blood test for Lyme disease. No founding year or founder names are disclosed in public materials, and ownership structure has not been specified.

The Lyme-ID test uses Inanovate's proprietary Bio-ID® technology with a single-step, modified two-tier methodology. Samples are collected at home using a pain-free upper arm device shipped in a kit that arrives within two days; the specimen is returned via prepaid packaging to the company's CLIA-certified laboratory, where results are posted to a secure portal in as little as 24 hours. The test is priced at $200 per kit.

Inanovate serves the medical diagnostics market, focusing on Lyme disease detection for consumers and potentially healthcare providers. The company cites CDC data noting over 300,000 new U.S. cases annually and positions its test for early-stage sensitivity where standard methods often miss infections.

Inanovate emphasizes that Lyme-ID achieved 81.7% sensitivity for Stage I Lyme and 100% for Stages II and III in FDA clinical trials using the CDC reference panel, outperforming standard two-tier and modified two-tier IgG tests. The firm highlights affordability, at-home convenience, and rapid turnaround as key differentiators.
